thread:
nora: Kickoff: proposal for a sequential handoff pattern for multi-region active/active. Goal: make rollouts predictable, minimize p95 blips, and guarantee no silent residency breaches. Looking for quick feedback on stabilization factors and operator safety.
sam: +1. I like sequencing: per-region slices applied in order with stabilisation checks between slices. Avoids simultaneous churn.
lee: Key pieces: prewarm (kv + model), slow ramp, stabilization window, optional two-phase commit to write final metadata. Suggest default windows but allow operator override.
rachel: Residency constraints: strict tenants must be fenced to local region always. Soft tenants get a leash (seconds) and explicit audit on any cross-region serve.
nora: Proposed default timings: prewarm=60s, ramp=5-10m (10%->75%), stabilize=10m. Stabilization requires metric flatness for last N seconds. Thoughts?
sam: Add a "stability_factor" parameter that scales required stability window by tenant QPS. High-QPS tenants need longer hysteresis. Eg stability = base * sqrt(qps).
lee: Good call. Router will need a per-tenant weight schedule and a fence token that prevents simultaneous rollouts. Add operator flag `--snapshot-id` for reproducibility.
nora: How to detect rollback triggers? My list: p95_delta > sla + 35ms for 3 consecutive minutes, 5xx_rate spike > 2x, remote_kv_miss_rate > 3x, model-incompat errors. Also detect "route-flicker" > 4 flips in 10m.
ops-bot: Runbook stub: /runbooks/sequential-handoff -> steps: snapshot, prewarm, ramp, stabilize, commit, rollback. Includes CLI examples for `--stagger` and `--snapshot-id`.
lee: Prefetch details: top-M keys by tenant (default M=100), plus model warmup: schedule <0.2 qps synthetic prompts sampled from top user prompts. Cost cap: abort prefetch if estimated GPU-seconds > tenant_budget. Tag billing to tenant.
nora: KMS constraints? kms-proxy: note.
kms-proxy: Envelope keys must not be transferred. For transient decrypts during leash window, issue ephemeral decrypt tokens scoped to audit and TTL <= leash_seconds. Tokens are single-use and logged.
legal: For EU-strict tenants: leash_seconds default 0. Any exception needs signed opt-in and an audit entry with operator_id and reason. Audit schema must include tenant_id, residency_policy, snapshot_id, rollout_id, operator_id, timestamp, and decision_reason. EU audits stored in-region.
sam: Implementation sketch: controller writes a rollout record with snapshot_id and desired phase. Router polls rollout record and implements weight schedule. Only when controller writes final commit state does router accept new steady-state routes (two-phase).
lee: Also need conflict resolution: if two rollouts target same tenant, controller uses `priority` in rollout record. Lower-priority rollout must pause and operator warned. CLI should support `--priority`.
nora: Model variant compatibility: catalog must include `compatibility_hash` and `degradation_rank`. Router prefers cheaper compatible variant (degradation ladder) before cross-region. This reduces cross-region needs.
ops-bot: Added CLI examples to runbook: `redwood rollout start --snapshot-id=42 --stagger=region-group --priority=10`. Also `redwood rollout abort --rollout-id=...`.
lee: Telemetry panels to add: remote_kv_miss_rate, prewarm_cost_sec, route_flicker_count, p95_delta_over_sla, model_variant_fallbacks. Alert thresholds per RFC.
kms-proxy: Operational note: ephemeral token issuance requires operator audit and an automated retained trace for 30d. We'll provide endpoint details.
legal: Approving audit fields; will send small wording tweaks but overall approach OK.
sam: Edge-case: partial-residency tenants (some blobs EU-only). Router should consult per-object residency hints. If object-level local only, refuse cross-region for that request and fall back to degradation ladder. Need metadata surface.
nora: Good point. We'll add `object_residency_hint` to tenant metadata and require router checks.
ops-bot: Canary started: seq-handoff-v1 -> eu-slice-1 -> bias=12% with snapshot-id=20230301. Prewarm running.
infra-bot: Canary telemetry: p95 stable, remote_kv_miss = 1.08x baseline, model_variant_fallbacks = 0. No flicker. Scaling next slice in 15m if stable.
nora: Next actions: sam -> draft RFC PR with stability_factor formula and controller state machine; lee -> prefetch script + cost guard; kms-proxy -> token API spec; legal -> final audit language. Target RFC early next week. If any metric trips, ops-bot please run rollback playbook and page oncall. Thanks all.
